edges.description: Without PAI-1, tissue plasminogen activator converts plasminogen to plasmin unchecked.
PAI-1 also restrains TGF-beta production in cardiomyocytes; its loss releases that restraint.
Clots formed at a surgical or traumatic wound are lysed early, so bleeding recurs after initial haemostasis.
Excess TGF-beta signalling drives collagen deposition in the myocardium.

edges.source: Hormonal Suppression for Heavy Menstrual Bleeding
Avoidance of Drugs Affecting Coagulation and High-Risk Activities

edges.limitations: The mice show increased clot lysis but no spontaneous or delayed rebleeding after injury, so the bleeding phenotype that defines the human disease is not reproduced.
Fibrosis appears in aged mice, while human homozygotes show it as young adults; the mouse mechanism data have not been confirmed in human myocardium.

nodes.description: Tranexamic acid or epsilon-aminocaproic acid treats bleeding episodes, including intracranial haemorrhage given intravenously, and is given prophylactically before surgery, dental procedures and childbirth. In pregnancy, oral antifibrinolytics are used for bleeding in the first two trimesters and continuously from 26 weeks through two weeks postpartum.

nodes.description: Biallelic null variants in SERPINE1 abolish PAI-1, a serine protease inhibitor (serpin) that is the primary inhibitor of tissue-type and urokinase-type plasminogen activators. In the first characterised kindred a frameshift in exon 4 left homozygotes with undetectable PAI-1 antigen. The DECREASED modifier records the loss of the inhibitor protein, not a measured change in its specific activity.

nodes.description: PAI-1 deficiency paradoxically causes cardiac-selective fibrosis. In PAI-1-null mice, ventricular myocytes are a source of TGF-beta, and loss of PAI-1 increases cardiomyocyte TGF-beta production and Smad signalling, with endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition contributing in aged hearts. iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes from homozygous Amish patients released more TGF-beta1 after angiotensin II. The human evidence is the imaging and iPSC data; the signalling detail comes from mice.

nodes.description: PAI-1 knockout mice are viable and fertile. They lyse clots faster and resist endotoxin-induced venous thrombosis, but they do not bleed spontaneously or rebleed after tail or caecum amputation. Aged knockouts develop cardiac-selective fibrosis.

Haemostatic clots form normally but are lysed prematurely by plasmin generated by unopposed tPA. In PAI-1-null mice the effect is a mild hyperfibrinolytic state without spontaneous bleeding; in patients it gives delayed bleeding after a haemostatic challenge, which is why spontaneous bleeding is absent.

nodes.description: Frameshift founder allele in the Old Order Amish of Indiana. Homozygotes have complete PAI-1 deficiency and a high rate of myocardial fibrosis. Heterozygous carriers do not bleed; in one Amish community they had longer leukocyte telomeres, lower fasting insulin, less diabetes and a longer life span.
